title: "Scripts & CI"
---

## Build & check scripts

`scripts/` holds four R helpers, plus a shared registry they all read. All are optional, a plain `quarto render` still works.

- Paths are resolved with the `here` package rather than requiring you to run from a specific working directory, and the template registry (`scripts/templates.R`) auto-discovers posters: either the multi-template layout shipped here (`templates/<dir>/*.qmd`, one per subdirectory), or,  if you deleted `templates/` and kept a single poster at the project's top level under any filename, that one file instead.

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `render-all.R` | Renders every discovered template to both formats, then runs every check below (including delegating to `check-contrast.R`); one command for the whole suite. Exits non-zero on failure, so it can be wired into CI or a pre-commit hook. Pass `--no-render` to check existing output without re-rendering. |
| `check-column-balance.R` | Measures how far down each Typst column the content actually reaches. Usable standalone: `Rscript scripts/check-column-balance.R templates/<name>/poster.pdf <num-columns>`. |
| `make-previews.R` | Regenerates `images/previews/preview-*.png` and `comparison.png` from the rendered PDFs. |
| `check-contrast.R` | Audits every foreground/background pair in the output against WCAG AA and AAA. Parses the palette, the stylesheets' own `color:`/`background:` rules (including both `linear-gradient()` stops), and each template's print footer YAML, so a re-color is re-audited rather than checked against a stale copy. Fails below AA, or below AAA with `--require-aaa`. See [Re-coloring the templates](theming.qmd#re-coloring-the-templates). |

`scripts/templates.R` is the shared registry of templates (column counts, print sizes, expected column-fill baselines) that the other three read, so adding a template to the multi-template layout is a one-line edit there; a template discovered outside that registry (e.g. a renamed single-poster fork) just runs without a column-balance baseline to compare against.

A `Makefile` wraps the common commands:

```bash
make render       # clear the stale Typst package cache, then render + check everything
make check        # run the checks against whatever output already exists (no render)
make clean-cache  # just clear .quarto/typst/packages (see the caching note below)
```

Every check in `render-all.R` exists because that failure actually happened once during development and was **invisible in the render log**:

- **pages**: a content edit overflowing onto a second Typst page; a poster must be exactly one page.
- **divider**: the web section divider disappearing from the HTML.
- **acknowledgments**: the raw-HTML-in-a-conditional-div bug described under [Notes / gotchas](#notes-gotchas), which dropped the acknowledgments, grant number, and References heading from print while the web version looked perfect.
- **ethics**: the Ethics & Broader Impact panel missing from either format (it is written once per format, so it can go missing from one).
- **balance**: a column emptying out relative to its measured baseline.
- **`#### after show rule`**: a `####` heading placed *above* the level-3 show rule described under [Notes / gotchas](#notes-gotchas). Typst show rules only affect what follows them, so such a heading silently keeps the package's "1) Heading:" run-in style.
- **contrast**: a palette edit dropping a color below WCAG AA, delegated to `check-contrast.R` so the same audit stays usable on its own.

### Continuous integration

`.github/workflows/posters.yml` runs these same scripts on push and pull request, in two deliberately separate jobs:

| Job | Runs | Why it is separate |
|---|---|---|
| `contrast` | `check-contrast.R --require-aaa` | Pure source parsing, no Quarto, no fonts, no rendering, so it is quick and its verdict is unambiguous. Every pair currently reaches AAA, so the strict gate is the meaningful one. |
| `render` | `render-all.R` (both formats for all three templates, plus every output check) | Needs the Typst toolchain and system libraries for `pdftools`/`magick`, which are the fragile parts. Keeping them apart means a toolchain or font problem is never mistaken for an accessibility regression. |

See [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AU-datascience/poster_templates/blob/main/AGENTS.md) for project orientation, the vendored extension's local patches, and the open fonts issue.

Two caveats worth knowing before you rely on it:

- **Quarto's release version matters.** Both workflows pin `quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2` to a specific Quarto version rather than tracking `release`; an unpinned run once picked up a pandoc/Typst-writer change that broke the institution-logo path substitution. The version lives in one file, `.quarto-version`, which each workflow reads into a step output before calling `setup@v2` -- so `posters.yml` and `docs.yml` cannot drift out of sync with each other the way two hardcoded copies could. See [Updating the pinned Quarto version](#updating-the-pinned-quarto-version) below for the bump procedure, and why the pin stays even though the specific bug it was protecting against is now also patched at the source.
- **Fonts change layout, and layout is measured.** `poster.typ` asks for `STIX Two Text`, and Quarto injects a `Source Sans 3` show rule for headings; both are now declared as brand font resources in `_brand.yml` (`source: google`), so Quarto fetches and caches them under `.quarto/typst/fonts/` at render time -- the runner needs no system fonts for the *print* render, and CI and local renders resolve the same faces by construction. (This is purely about print/CI reproducibility; see [Theming & Brand](theming.qmd#brand.yml-and-your-workflow) for what the same `_brand.yml` declaration does -- and doesn't -- deliver for the `html` output.)

#### Updating the pinned Quarto version

Bump `.quarto-version` deliberately rather than letting either workflow drift to a new release silently:

1. Install the candidate Quarto release locally.
2. Run `make check-quarto-version` to confirm `quarto --version` matches the release you just installed (it fails loudly on a mismatch, so you know you are about to test the version you think you are).
3. Run `make render` (renders every template and all output checks) and, if you touched `docs-src/`, `quarto render docs-src` too. Inspect the rendered PDFs/HTML, not just the check output -- the balance/contrast checks catch some regressions, not all of them.
4. Only once that looks right, edit `.quarto-version` and commit. Both `posters.yml` and `docs.yml` read the same file, so one edit updates both workflows.

**Why the pin stays, even after the path fix.** `_extensions/quarto-ext/poster/typst-show.typ` now strips a stray leading backslash from the substituted institution-logo path defensively (see [Notes / gotchas](#notes-gotchas)), which patches the *specific* bug that originally motivated pinning. That is not a reason to switch either workflow back to tracking `release`: the pin's job is to make a render on a given commit reproducible run to run, and it was already carrying that weight for other reasons before this bug was ever found -- e.g. the font-resolution differences discussed in [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/AU-datascience/poster_templates/blob/main/AGENTS.md). A future pandoc/Typst-writer change breaking something else entirely (a different substitution, color handling, heading numbering) would be just as invisible under `release` as this one was, and there is no way to defensively patch a bug that hasn't happened yet. Tracking `release` trades a small, bounded maintenance cost (the four steps above, only needed when you actually want a newer Quarto) for an unbounded and unpredictable one (CI failing on an unrelated commit because GitHub's runner picked up a new Quarto release overnight).

This documentation site itself is a separate, nested Quarto website project: sources live in `docs-src/` (its own `docs-src/_quarto.yml`), rendering to `docs/`. GitHub Pages (Settings -> Pages: branch main, `/docs`) serves that committed `docs/` folder directly; there's no publish step in CI; 

- `.github/workflows/docs.yml` renders `docs-src/` fresh and then diffs the result against the committed `docs/`, independent of the two jobs above. 
- If they differ, someone edited `docs-src/` (or an image `copy-images.sh` pulls in) without re-rendering, a stale `/docs` is otherwise invisible in a PR diff, since `docs-src/*.qmd` changes review fine on their own. 
- After editing anything under `docs-src/`, re-render and commit the result: `quarto render docs-src`.

## Notes / gotchas

- The vendored `_extensions/quarto-ext/poster` has local patches. If you re-install/update the extension, re-apply all of them:
  - `poster.typ` accepts the institution logo as already-loaded Typst `content` (loaded once in `typst-show.typ`) rather than a bare path string, because Typst packages cannot read files outside their own package directory (see the `_univ_logo_img` handling in `typst-show.typ`).
  - `poster.typ` / `typst-show.typ` add a `footer-text-color` format option (defaults to white) so the footer text stays legible against
    dark `footer-color` values. Set it to a dark color if you pick a light footer background (see `01-classic-academic`'s `footer-text-color: "25406A"`).
  - `biblio.typ` (a new template-partial, registered in `_extension.yml`) sets `title: none` on the generated `#bibliography(...)` call, so Typst's own default "Bibliography" heading doesn't duplicate each template's own `#### References` heading.
  - `poster.typ` also scales the footer's font sizes down (never up) on posters narrower than the extension's documented 36in default, so the footer row (URL + text + emails, packed with `h(1fr)` spacers) doesn't wrap outside its colored background block on narrower prints like `03-minimal-story`'s 24in width.
  - `typst-show.typ` strips a stray leading backslash from the substituted institution-logo path before calling `image()` on it, defending against a pandoc/Typst-writer bug that once inserted one and broke the render with "path must not contain a backslash" (see [Updating the pinned Quarto version](scripts-and-ci.qmd#updating-the-pinned-quarto-version)). It is a no-op when the path is already clean, so it is safe regardless of Quarto version.
  - Because Quarto caches the vendored local Typst package under each project's `.quarto/typst/packages/local/typst-poster/`, edits to `poster.typ` only take effect after that cached copy is refreshed (delete `.quarto/` or copy the updated file over it, or just run `make render`). A plain `quarto render` will silently keep using the stale cached version.
- Every template's `poster-typst` format sets **`fig-format: png`**. Without it, Typst's default (`fig-format: svg`) asks R's Cairo graphics device to render each plot, which can fail with a missing X11/Cairo shared-library error on machines without XQuartz (common on Apple Silicon macOS, and on Linux without `libcairo2-dev`).
    - Installing XQuartz/`libcairo` dev packages fixes it at the source; `fig-format: png` sidesteps it by using R's built-in PNG device instead, at a small cost in image sharpness for print.
- **Never put a raw `<hr>` (or other raw HTML) inside a `::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}` div.** Doing so silently discards *every element after it* in the Typst output -- the templates lost their section divider, the entire Acknowledgments block (advisor, grant number, code/data link), and the `#### References` heading from the printed PDF, while still rendering fine on the web. Use a ```` ```{=html} ```` raw block instead, which HTML picks up and Typst ignores cleanly.
- **Column balance:** the shipped samples do not fill their columns evenly, and that is accepted slack rather than a bug -- `02-modern-cards` reaches ~44% down column 1 vs ~82% down column 2, and `03-minimal-story` ends ~79% down its single column. The Evidence figure is one ~10in-tall indivisible block, so moving `02`'s `#colbreak()` past it only inverts the gap (measured 91%/29%, a wider spread). Real content is the remedy. Baselines live in `scripts/templates.R`; `render-all.R` fails on a *drop* of more than 10 points from them.
- **Web banner contrast:** the title banner is a gradient, so banner text must clear its *lighter* stop, not just the dark one. The original `$au-light-blue` author/date color measured 6.97:1 on navy but only 3.59:1 on the `$au-blue` stop, a WCAG AA failure. All banner text is now plain white on a darkened light stop (`$au-blue-banner`, 7.21:1), and link and grey body text were darkened to clear AAA too. See [Re-coloring the templates](theming.qmd#re-coloring-the-templates), and run `Rscript scripts/check-contrast.R` after any color change.
- **`####` headings arrive as Typst level *3*, not level 4.** Quarto maps markdown `##` to `=`, shifting every heading up one level, so the closing-matter headings land on the poster package's level-3 style: a numbered, italic, colon-terminated run-in that prints as "1) Acknowledgments:" and reads like a numbered list item. Each template overrides this with a `#show heading.where(level: 3)` rule in the raw Typst block just above `#### Acknowledgments`, defined *after* the package's own `show heading` rule so it takes precedence. A `####` heading placed earlier in the poster still gets the package's run-in style, since Typst show rules only apply to content after them.
- **Font-size hierarchy is not automatic.** The poster package defaults `title-font-size` to 48pt and `authors-font-size` to 36pt, and derives level-1 headings as `body-font-size + 16`. If you shrink `title-font-size` to fit a long title (as `03-minimal-story` needs to at 24in wide), lower `authors-font-size` too and keep the title above `body-font-size + 16`, or the author line and section headings will print *larger* than the title.
- `.quarto/`, rendered `*.pdf`/`*.typ`/`poster.html`, and `*_files/` directories are gitignored as build output.
